The reward must belong to the operator domain H as recorded in footnote 3; its proposed projection alternative is not inserted into the original formula. Rank-one operators and finite sums express C_hat/C_cross_hat, but the latter need not be self-adjoint. Positive lambda_n alone is not a proved invertibility certificate for the full operator. Preserve the potentially infinite-dimensional setting, n>0 and the theorem's actual parameter regime.

variant_reviews.comparison: Form sum_{j=1}^d Pi_j composed with F as an ambient-space operator; starProjection has the correct codomain, unlike a projection whose output is only the subspace subtype. Under the eigenspace properties this equals the sum of lambda_j Pi_j over the retained distinct eigenvalues. The archived Pi_j projects onto the whole eigenspace for the j-th distinct eigenvalue, whereas the dotted sequence counts eigenvectors with multiplicity. Thus the formula can retain more than d individual components unless the appropriate simple-spectrum conditions apply; do not replace it with an arbitrary basis-vector cutoff. Finite nonzero eigenspaces of the compact self-adjoint operator admit the needed projections. The empirical version uses the sequential estimator's own corresponding eigenspaces, not fixed population projections, and retains its eta/index/denominator issues. Spectral completeness alone does not provide ordered eigenvalue selection, uniform eigengaps or the trace-class process limit and differentiability arguments used downstream.
